newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - EU probes Credit Lyonnais buyback of SDBO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU probes Credit Lyonnais buyback of SDBO.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday that French bank Credit Lyonnais may have received more subsidy than approved for its rescue plan through the repurchase of a former banking unit.
In a statement the Commission said it had evidence that the bank had paid 123 million French francs ($23.88 million) less than it ought for the Societe de Banque Occidentale (SDBO).
SDBO, banker for French entrepreneur-turned-politician Bernard Tapie, was transferred in 1995 into CDR, a state-backed vehicle created to rid the Lyonnais of its loss-making assets.
This was part of a July 1995 three-year restructuring plan for Lyonnais involving a maximum 45 billion French franc ($8.75 billion) in state subsidies.
Under its terms, the troubled bank -- which was once Europe's largest -- could buy back some of the assets formerly divested into CDR at the price paid by the latter or at market value if higher.

But the Commission said that Lyonnais only paid 50 million francs for SDBO, despite CDR having injected 274.5 million francs into the bank at the beginning of 1996. It said conditions under which the transaction took place completely lacked transparency.
"There was no tender and only seven potential buyers -- all of them French -- were consulted with very short deadlines for reply," the statement said,

"An independent estimate put the average value of SDBO after recapitalisation at 173 million francs," the Commission added. It concluded, critically, that potential buyers were not informed of the CDR capital injection.
The Commission gave France a month to reply.
In a separate statement, the Commission cleared a 2.8 billion franc capital injection in also state-controlled French financial group GAN, following the assessment of a recovery plan for the company.
The Commission took into consideration the problems encountered by GAN in the banking sector due to a deep crisis in the French property sector.
It also looked with keen eyes at a pledge by the French government to privatise GAN -- which is usually the only guarantee that subsidy flows will stop.

But these were not the only French state aid cases the Commission had to discuss at its weekly meeting on Wednesday. It also questionned ruthlessly a rescue plan for regional bank Societe Marseillaise de Credit, which Commission sources said involves 2.0 billion francs. The bank is set for privatisation. There was no official statement on this case.

Finally the EU executive, which must clear all subsidies in the Union before they are actually paid, also started a probe into a proposal by the Belgian authorities to salvage loss-making steel company Forges de Clabecq. $1 = 5.14 French francs ($1=5.151 French Franc)
